brief_drift: The “PRODUCT LAUNCH” and “Today, we’re introducing Tally” framing drifts from the brief by presenting the documented capability as a new launch without evidence of novelty.

edits.line: PRODUCT LAUNCH / Today, we’re introducing Tally: an online form builder that can send new submissions into your automation workflows through webhooks.
edits.problem: The combined framing makes an unsupported time-sensitive launch claim, even though the evidence establishes only an existing documented capability.
edits.fix: Remove the novelty claim while preserving the early orientation that Tally is an online form builder and that webhooks send new submissions into automation workflows.

edits.line: The webhook documentation covers the capability, delivery details, and timeout so you can decide whether it fits the workflows your agency builds.
edits.problem: “Delivery details” is vague and can suggest that the documentation answers payload-format, authentication, replay, or response-handling questions that the supplied evidence does not establish.
edits.fix: Limit the promised inspection payoff to the supported questions: new-submission delivery, event and response inspection, failed-attempt retries, and the 10-second endpoint constraint.

summary: Keep the documented webhook proposition, but remove the unsupported launch framing and bound the documentation promise to the implementation details the evidence actually supports.
